edit.description: matchesAny/globToRegex (473-483) move to a shared home so a second consumer can call them - src/paths.ts is the path-shaped module that already exists; builtinGates imports them back
receives the glob matcher as its shared home

ship detection (1596-1599) matches commitTouchedPaths against declaredPaths via the shared matcher instead of Array.includes - the same semantics the entry-scope write guard at 2060 already applies to the same declaredPaths(entry) list
the agreement pin - a glob-declaring entry whose commit touches a real matching file ships instead of landing channel-only
changelogGate requires a line on any src/-touching commit

summary: Ship detection compares declared paths to commit paths with literal equality while the entry-scope write guard glob-matches the same list - a glob-declaring entry lands on trunk but never drains.

per.section: The fix lands at the mechanism

tests.asserts: a fanout entry declaring a glob (e.g. nodes/territory-*.json) whose worktree commit touches a real matching file (nodes/territory-01.json) is reported merged and removed from pending.json - fails on the pre-fix tree, where Array.includes returns false and the entry is logged channel-only while its commit stays on trunk

acceptance: One glob matcher serves both the entry-scope write guard and ship detection; a glob-declaring entry that touches a matching file ships and drains; a commit touching only channel paths still lands channel-only; tsc/vitest green.
notes: Downstream report (0.9.0 dist), re-verified here. declaredPaths(entry) has two consumers that both judge real commit paths and disagree: Dispatcher.ts:2060 hands it to writablePathsGate as globs; Dispatcher.ts:1596-1599 compares it with Array.includes. Effect is a non-draining loop - commit on trunk, entry still pickable, next tick redoes landed work. matchesAny is module-private today, so sharing needs the move.

edit.description: add optional shouldRun?(ctx: TickContext): boolean per §8 - decline before invocation, undeclared unchanged

consult phase.shouldRun before rendering/invoking (singleton ~1075, fanout path); false -> no agent call, no commit, baton-sleep/handoff still run (~1112-1116), verdict carries a declined fact as a TickVerdict/TickOutcome sibling (tipMoved's precedent ~1104-1146), never a 5th NoCommitMode variant
new shouldRun section beside handoff (~169), leads with the yield-to-pickable-work case, states the synchronous/cheap contract

summary: Phase.shouldRun: an optional predicate the dispatcher consults before invoking the agent, so a chain can decline a tick without spending one (§8).

tests.asserts: shouldRun=false on a phase: a stub agent that throws if called never runs, no commit lands, handoff still runs (baton sleeps/wakes as usual); shouldRun=true is byte-identical to a phase declaring none; a chain declaring shouldRun nowhere reproduces today's tick counts exactly; the declined outcome reads distinct from voluntary-bail in the tick verdict

acceptance: A phase whose shouldRun returns false produces no agent invocation, no commit, and still hands off; true or undeclared is unchanged behavior; declined is distinguishable from voluntary-bail and from hibernation in the verdict.
notes: TickContext already carries pending/assignedEntry (Phase.ts:32-47) - no new plumbing. Follow tipMoved's sibling-fact precedent on TickVerdict/TickOutcome rather than growing NoCommitMode.

edit.description: createWorktree (~2195-2242): the worktree path's directory component derives from a length-bounded name (truncated slugify(entry.tag) + short hash of the full tag) per §9; branch (~2203) and priorAttemptKey (~2253) keep the untruncated slug - only the fs directory is bounded

remove the win32 skipIf on TAG-LENGTH-BOUND-AGREEMENT-PIN (~6475) and the unconditional skip on PRIORATTEMPT-WIN32-PATH-TOTAL-LIMIT (~6970) so both run on every platform; add a case pinning two tags sharing a long common prefix to distinct worktree directories
Changed: worktree dirname length bound line per §9

summary: createWorktree derives a length-bounded worktree directory name instead of the raw tag slug, so any schema-valid tag provisions its fanout worktree on win32 (§9).

tests.asserts: a TAG_MAX_LENGTH-tag fanout entry provisions and ships on win32 (no skip); two tags sharing a long common prefix get distinct worktree directories; the full tag still appears in the commit message and the §5 prior-attempt record; PRIORATTEMPT-WIN32-PATH-TOTAL-LIMIT round-trips on every platform

acceptance: TAG-LENGTH-BOUND-AGREEMENT-PIN and PRIORATTEMPT-WIN32-PATH-TOTAL-LIMIT run unskipped on every platform and pass; distinct-prefix tags get distinct worktree dirs; the full tag is unchanged everywhere else it's read.
notes: Bound is an engine constant (not a chain knob) sized so <wtBase>/<namespace>/<dir> clears git's ~200-char win32 ceiling. Resolves the parked 'schema-valid tag unshippable on win32' open question - closed this tick.

new.description: vendored type-only StandardSchemaV1 declaration per §11 - no runtime code, structurally unifies with zod's own ~standard

edit.description: EntryExtensionField.schema: StandardSchemaV1 (was z.ZodTypeAny, ~152); composePendingList (~224-248) adapts each declared validator via ~standard.validate into an engine-instance schema - value-preserving, re-raises issues at entry-indexed/composed paths, refuses loudly (naming the field) a validator whose Promise result would read as accepting everything; tag intersection (~244) composes against the adapted refinement
agreement gate drives real parsePending over hand-written ~standard validators (no zod) per §11 acceptance
§10: declared type is a Standard Schema (~1182), zod example kept as an implementation not the contract; note a chain's own .parse() (~1235) is untouched
record the retired zod-copy-skew TypeError; no migration step - existing zod schemas already satisfy StandardSchemaV1
Changed: entryExtension validator protocol line per §11

summary: entryExtension field validators declare a Standard Schema (~standard) instead of a zod schema; the engine adapts rather than merges chain-constructed zod objects (§11).

per.section: 11. The extension seam takes a validator, not a zod schema

tests.asserts: hand-written ~standard validators (no zod) through real parsePending: a conforming entry accepts; a field violation rejects carrying the foreign validator's own message at the entry-indexed path, a nested one at [0].per.path; a chain tag refinement narrows and cannot widen the core floor; an undeclared key rejects; a duplicate tag rejects; a vacuity pin proves the foreign validator was actually invoked, not skipped past

a declared validator that supplies a value for an absent key materializes it in the parsed entry (chain.ts's tests:.default([]) case) - a verdict-only adapter fails this while passing every case above
an async validator's declaration is refused naming the field, rather than accepting the entry vacuously

acceptance: composePendingList/parsePending accept any ~standard validator, not only zod; zod stays a private engine dependency (not peer, not re-exported); a chain declaring zod schemas parses byte-identically to today.
notes: Closes the parked 'zod is a dependency, not a peer' open question with a different disposition than its own recommendation (peerDependency) - the spec instead removes the merge via an adapter (engine-boundary.md: holding the object reaches past what mechanics consume).
